parts.prompt: Find the speed of the particle and its acceleration vector at $$t = 1.5$$.
Find the slope of the line tangent to the path of the particle at $$t = 1.5$$.
Find the position of the particle at $$t = 3$$.

rubric.criterion: Uses the initial position with the integral of each component.

parts.prompt: Find the total distance traveled by the particle over $$0 \leq t \leq 3$$.
Find the slope of the slope-field segment at each of the points $$(-1, 2)$$, $$(0, 3)$$, $$(1, 0)$$ and $$(2, 1)$$.
Write an equation for the line tangent to the graph of $$f$$ at $$x = 1$$, and use it to approximate $$f(1.2)$$.

rubric.criterion: Finds the slope at the point and writes the tangent line.

parts.prompt: Find $$\frac{d^2y}{dx^2}$$ in terms of $$x$$ and $$y$$. Is the approximation in part (b) an overestimate or an underestimate? Explain.

rubric.criterion: Uses the sign of the second derivative at the point to conclude.
rubric.example: At $$(1, 0)$$, $$\frac{d^2y}{dx^2} = -6$$, so f is concave down and the tangent line lies above the curve: an overestimate.

parts.prompt: Find the particular solution $$y = f(x)$$ with $$f(1) = 0$$.

questions.title: Rate of people entering a park

parts.prompt: Use the data to estimate $$P'(7)$$. Show the computations and indicate units.

rubric.criterion: Uses a difference quotient on the interval containing the time.

parts.prompt: Use a trapezoidal sum with the four subintervals shown in the table to approximate $$\int_0^{12} P(t)\,dt$$. Explain the meaning of this integral in the context of the problem.

rubric.criterion: Sets up the trapezoidal sum with unequal widths.

rubric.example: The total number of people who enter the park during the first 12 minutes.

parts.prompt: Must there be a time $$c$$, for $$3 < c < 9$$, such that $$P'(c) = 0$$? Justify your answer.

rubric.criterion: Answers yes, citing the Mean Value Theorem (or Rolle's Theorem) with its conditions.
rubric.example: Yes. $$P$$ is differentiable (so continuous), and $$P(3) = P(9) = 62$$. By the Mean Value Theorem there is a $$c$$ with $$P'(c) = \frac{62 - 62}{6} = 0$$.

parts.prompt: Must there be a time $$t$$, for $$0 < t < 3$$, at which $$P(t) = 59$$? Justify your answer.

rubric.criterion: Answers yes, citing the Intermediate Value Theorem and continuity.
rubric.example: Yes. $$P$$ is continuous, and $$59$$ is between $$P(0) = 57$$ and $$P(3) = 62$$, so the IVT guarantees such a $$t$$.

parts.prompt: Find the x-coordinates of all relative extrema of $$f$$, and classify each as a relative maximum or relative minimum. Justify your answer.

rubric.criterion: Classifies both with a sign-change justification.
rubric.example: $$f'$$ changes from positive to negative at $$1$$ (relative maximum) and from negative to positive at $$3$$ (relative minimum).

parts.prompt: On what intervals is the graph of $$f$$ concave down? Give a reason.

rubric.criterion: Gives the interval with a reason based on $$f''$$.

parts.prompt: Find the absolute maximum value of $$f$$ on the closed interval $$[-1, 4]$$. Justify your answer.

rubric.criterion: Evaluates $$f$$ at the critical points and endpoints.
Recognizes the form 0/0 and applies L'Hospital's Rule (twice, or once with $$f'(1) = 0$$).

parts.prompt: Find the interval of convergence of the series. Show the work that leads to your answer.

rubric.criterion: Analyzes both endpoints with a test.
rubric.example: At $$x = 4$$: $$\sum \frac{(-1)^{n+1}}{n}$$ converges (alternating series test). At $$x = -4$$: $$-\sum \frac{1}{n}$$ diverges (harmonic).

parts.prompt: Find the first three nonzero terms and the general term of the Maclaurin series for $$f'(x)$$. Then write $$f'(x)$$ as a rational function.
Use the first two nonzero terms of the series to approximate $$f(1)$$. Show that this approximation differs from $$f(1)$$ by less than $$0.008$$.

rubric.criterion: Uses the alternating series error bound with justification.
rubric.example: The series at $$x = 1$$ alternates with terms decreasing to 0, so the error is at most the third term, $$\frac{1}{3\cdot 64} = \frac{1}{192}$$.
